logMd:
#### plugin87/ux-ui-agent-skills -- 11 rejected skills (inspected 2026-08-26)

See a11y-audit.json for shared repo-level evidence (HEAD SHA 2ffb677aa02b225c8a3da1b7f31d9ebb7c38f1dd, 811 stars, license resolved via package.json SPDX MIT / author plugin87, full 17-skill enumeration, and the note that scripts/, workflows/, taste/ were confirmed present via the Contents API after an initial recursive-tree fetch silently dropped them). Of the 17 skills enumerated, 6 were vendored (a11y-audit, design-review, design-tokens, brandkit, figma-integration, migrate-design-system) plus token-build as a 7th, filling 7 of the at-most-8 slots; the 11 listed here were not vendored. Reasons split into three groups: (1) apply-aesthetic and image-to-code depend on a 138-file repo-root design-systems/library catalog that is disproportionate to bundle for one skill each; (2) design-code, design-component, design-qa, governance, redesign and ux-writing are near-duplicates (uniqueness 0-1) of skills already in the registry or, for ux-writing, of the stronger dedicated candidate inspected in the same batch; (3) performance falls below the relevance>=2 vendor threshold (it is frontend engineering, not a design activity); prototype has a real methodological difference from the registry's existing 'prototype' skill but collides on the exact id string, flagged rather than force-renamed. All had clean security (no scripts beyond the already-reviewed shared ones) and the same package.json-SPDX MIT license as the vendored picks -- none were rejected on license or security grounds, all on relevance/uniqueness/cap grounds.
